skill.name: storage-debug-instrumentation
skill.description: Guides implementation of internal debugging and observability tools for PostgreSQL, ChromaDB, FastAPI startup metrics, and a Next.js debug dashboard.
skill.summary: Add internal storage diagnostics, startup metrics, drift checks, and a debug dashboard for backend troubleshooting.
skill.author: BenderFendor

security_audit.summary: Most static backtick findings are false positives caused by Markdown code spans, and the localhost URLs are verification examples. The real issue is the skill design: it asks users to expose raw storage inspection and startup diagnostics without required access controls. These routes need admin gating and redaction before production use.

remediation.issue: Debug endpoints may expose raw storage and operational data.
remediation.suggestion: Require admin authentication, authorization checks, and environment gating for every /debug route. Disable these routes by default in production.

remediation.issue: Storage inspection responses may include sensitive article content or metadata.
remediation.suggestion: Redact article bodies, sensitive metadata, hostnames, ports, and version details unless each field is required for diagnosis.

remediation.issue: Debug tooling lacks explicit operational controls.
remediation.suggestion: Add pagination limits, audit logging, rate limits, and clear deployment guidance for internal-only diagnostics.

content.value_statement: Storage drift and slow startup phases can be hard to diagnose across PostgreSQL, ChromaDB, and a Next.js frontend. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to add internal metrics, inspection routes, and a debug dashboard.
actual_capabilities: Guides creation of startup timing metrics for backend initialization phases.
Defines paginated inspection helpers for PostgreSQL article records.
Defines ChromaDB article listing and ID enumeration for drift checks.
Specifies FastAPI debug endpoints for startup, database, ChromaDB, and drift reports.
Specifies a Next.js debug dashboard with tabs, filters, pagination, and summary cards.
Includes verification steps for local endpoints and dashboard behavior.
limitations: Does not include authentication, authorization, or production access controls.
Provides implementation instructions, not tested source files in this package.
Assumes a FastAPI backend, PostgreSQL, ChromaDB, and Next.js frontend.
May expose sensitive article content if implemented without redaction.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Storage Drift
use_cases.description: Compare PostgreSQL mappings with ChromaDB IDs to find missing and dangling entries.

use_cases.title: Measure Startup Bottlenecks
use_cases.description: Capture phase durations and metadata during backend startup to locate slow initialization steps.

use_cases.title: Build an Internal Debug Dashboard
use_cases.description: Create a Next.js page that combines storage browsers, filters, metrics, and drift summaries.

prompt_templates.title: Add Startup Metrics
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for backend timing data.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to add startup metrics to my FastAPI backend. Record each initialization phase and expose an internal timeline endpoint.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect Storage State
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for database and vector store visibility.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to add paginated inspection helpers for PostgreSQL and ChromaDB. Include filters, counts, and safe preview fields.

prompt_templates.title: Create Debug Dashboard
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for a frontend diagnostic view.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to build a Next.js debug page. Show startup metrics, ChromaDB entries, database rows, and storage drift samples.

prompt_templates.title: Harden Debug Instrumentation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to implement the debug tooling with admin authentication, environment gating, redaction, pagination limits, and audit logging.

output_examples.input: A user asks for startup diagnostics in a FastAPI service.
output_examples.output: A plan that adds a startup metrics service, records each boot phase, and returns a timeline for internal review.

output_examples.input: A user asks to compare PostgreSQL articles with ChromaDB vectors.
output: A drift report design with missing and dangling entry counts.
Pagination and filters for inspecting samples safely.

output_examples.input: A user asks for a storage debugging interface.
output_examples.output: A dashboard specification with tabs for startup, ChromaDB, database rows, and drift status.

best_practices: Protect every debug endpoint with admin authentication and environment gating.
Redact article text, metadata, hostnames, ports, and version details unless they are required.
Keep pagination limits small and log access to debug views.
anti_patterns: Do not expose /debug routes publicly or enable them by default in production.
Do not return full article bodies when short previews answer the diagnostic question.
Do not run local verification commands without user approval in managed agent environments.

faq.question: What systems does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets FastAPI services that use PostgreSQL, ChromaDB, and a Next.js frontend.

faq.question: Does it include ready-to-run source code?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation guidance and verification checklists for adding diagnostics.

faq.question: Is it safe for production use?
faq.answer: Only with admin authentication, environment gating, and redaction. The base instructions do not include those controls.

faq.question: What data can the dashboard show?
faq.answer: It can show startup metrics, database rows, ChromaDB entries, drift samples, filters, and summary counts.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is written for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: What should teams review before adoption?
faq.answer: Review endpoint access, sensitive fields, pagination limits, logging, and production deployment settings.
